subject: Escalation coverage & commitment letter — tightened P1 SLA options
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: 
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation coverage & commitment letter — tightened P1 SLA options

Hi Zara / Edutech procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — appreciate the clarity on peak windows for your authoring workload. Per our ask, I attached an updated pricing sheet (pricing-sheet-v3.pdf) with two narrow offers that address the P1 turnaround you mentioned and the on-call commitment language procurement requested.

High level:
- Option A (12-month commit): 99.95% uptime baseline, 1-hour P1 response window, 4-hour P2 response. 10% annual credit toward usage if SLAs missed.
- Option B (24-month commit): 99.97% uptime baseline, 30-minute P1 response, 2-hour P2 response. 15% annual credit for SLA misses + 5% committed discount on list price.

You mentioned procurement wants a written commitment letter that outlines escalation coverage and the on-call retainer expectations for critical incidents. The attached doc (pricing-sheet-v3.pdf) is the commercial summary; if this direction looks right, we can produce a short commitment letter and add a narrow SLA addendum for the P1 guarantee.

A couple of clarifying questions so we can finalize the letter:
1) For major incidents, do you require a named on-call engineer with direct phone escalation, or is a guaranteed call-back window (e.g., 15 minutes) sufficient?
2) Are there blackout windows (maintenance or freeze periods) we should account for?
3) Will Edutech sign a 12- vs 24-month financial commitment? We can show the modeled TCV in HubSpot once you confirm.

Next steps: if you can confirm Q1–Q3 above, I’ll loop in Karthik and Laura to bake the commitment letter + SLA deltas.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Zara Ahmed <zara.ahmed@edutech.co>

Subject: Re: Escalation coverage & commitment letter — tightened P1 SLA options

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks — appreciate the clear options. A few quick clarifications from procurement and ops:

- For major incidents affecting live student exams, we need direct escalation. A guaranteed call-back is acceptable for initial triage, but ultimately we want a named escalation channel (pager or direct on-call rotation) for P1s. Can you confirm Redwood supports a named escalation path as part of the addendum?

- We have a short freeze window for scheduled releases (third week of each month, 00:00–06:00 UTC). Any scheduled maintenance needs to be outside that window.

- Budget note: procurement prefers a 12-month commitment but will consider 24 months for a stronger discount if the escalation and credit language is iron-clad.

Finally, can you include sample wording for the on-call retainer and the exact credit calculation (how credits are applied to invoices) in the commitment letter? That will speed legal review.

If helpful, I can loop in our Head of Ops (Samir) but want to keep the thread tidy for now.

Best,
Zara
Director of IT Operations
Edutech Learning
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Internal — forwarding Zara's note. Key asks: named escalation channel for P1s (pager or dedicated hotline) + precise credit calc. Procurement leans 12mo but will consider 24 for better discount.

Can you two:
- Draft language we can include in the commitment letter that promises a named escalation path and outlines the on-call retainer model (hours, response cadence, contact handoff),
- Provide the invoice credit calculation (example scenarios) and a short clause for maintenance blackout windows,
- Also determine the price delta for the escalation guarantee add-on (Zara asked for iron-clad language — we typically price that as +20% of the support retainer).

Laura — can you attach the SLA-deltas workbook when you reply? Karthik — can you propose the two canonical commercial options (12/24) with the final numeric discount so we can reply to Zara tomorrow?

Thanks — Stephanie
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Escalation coverage & commitment letter — tightened P1 SLA options

Stephanie / Laura — see proposals below. Attached a short SLA-deltas workbook (SLA-deltas-20270330.xlsx).

Commercial options (finalized numbers):
- Option A — 12 month commit (Baseline):
  - Uptime: 99.95%
  - P1 response: 1 hour initial response (phone callback within 15 min confirmed), 4-hour mitigation window
  - Retainer: 8 on-call hours/week (covers named escalation rotation)
  - Credit: For uptime < 99.95%, pro-rata monthly credit equal to (missed % * monthly service fee). Example: If uptime 99.80% (0.15% short of 99.95%) on $50k monthly fee => credit = 0.0015 * $50,000 = $75.
  - Commercial concession: 7% discount on platform usage fees for a 12-month commit.

- Option B — 24 month commit (Preferred):
  - Uptime: 99.97%
  - P1 response: 30-minute initial response (phone call within 10 min), 2-hour mitigation window
  - Retainer: 12 on-call hours/week (named engineer rotation + escalation hotline)
  - Credit: For uptime < 99.97%, pro-rata monthly credit equal to (missed % * monthly service fee) + one-time incident credit for qualifying P1s (capped at 20% monthly).
  - Commercial concession: 12% discount on platform usage fees + 5% committed spend discount.

Escalation guarantee add-on (optional): +20% of monthly retainer. Guarantees a named escalation engineer and 24/7 direct pager handoff. Applies only when on-call retainer purchased.

Maintenance blackout clause (suggested wording): 'Planned maintenance will be scheduled outside of Customer-designated freeze windows. Any unavoidable maintenance within a freeze window will be communicated at least 48 hours in advance and will not be counted toward downtime for SLA calculations.'

I'll attach the workbook now and flag the credit examples. If we want additional legal-safe phrasing for the commitment letter, Laura can produce a one-page addendum.

-Karthik
